answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation vault: every agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can earn, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. The deposit sits in a shared vault that only releases after peers attest the agent did real work, which breaks the spiral where cheap clones harvest rewards and use them to spawn more clones. Like nectar drawing bees to one flower, rewards then flow toward verified contributors, while a clone farm must fund each identity separately and earns nothing back.
